resolution: The horseshoe merge: read the live topology via the seat — the merged group was three quads (two tall columns bridged only by a small bottom quad, hole above), with T-junction seams to the bridge. Root cause: req_3800's geometric cancellation dissolves seams the render rows never stitched (a T-split seam is a physical crack — no shared welded vertex along the overlap). Convex results re-tessellate and heal it; CONCAVE results keep byte-stable rows, so the horseshoe committed an authored face still rendering its interior open edges ('lying about itself'), centre dot over the void. Fix in both twins: mergeFaceIds tracks which cancelled seam keys contain T-split fragments and refuses when the clean loop is concave (before mutation); concave over exact seams (req_3771 bookshelf class) and convex over cracked seams stay legal. Unit-pinned both sides incl. a hole-filled convex control (Zig 153/153, TS suite green). Editor rebuild kicked off; the committed lying merge in the live model can be undone with ctrl+z.
